In Switzerland the lesser stag beetle is still quite common, while the stag beetle has become rare. Anyone who leaves old tree stumps and woodpiles lying in the garden creates habitat for these beetles.

begriffe.erklaerung: The beetle family to which the stag beetle and the lesser stag beetle belong.
Dead wood that serves many animals as food and shelter.
The young form of an insect, which looks quite different from the adult animal.
The chewing tools of beetles, lengthened into antlers in the male stag beetle.

gewusst: Because of its size and colour, the lesser stag beetle is often mistaken for a female stag beetle.
Its larvae often live longer than the finished beetle.

teile.einleitung: A retriever is a dog that was bred to find things and bring them back carefully. This bringing back is called retrieving. Well-known retrievers are the Labrador Retriever and the Golden Retriever.
wichtigste: When a dog brings back a ball or a stick, this is called retrieving.
Retrievers are named after what they do: “retrieve” means to fetch back.
They were bred to fetch birds shot during a hunt.
They carry the game in a soft mouth without damaging it.
Many retrievers love water and like to swim.
The Labrador and the Golden Retriever are the best-known breeds.
Because of their friendly nature they often work as guide dogs for the blind.

abschnitte.text: The word **retrieving** in German, “Apportieren”, comes from the French “apporter”, which means to bring. The dog fetches an object and brings it back to its person. Many dogs do this quite naturally when playing with a ball or stick. In retrievers this joy is especially strong, because they were bred for it over many generations.

Most retrievers come from **Great Britain** and North America. Hunters needed dogs that would fetch shot ducks and other birds out of water or dense undergrowth. The dog has to wait patiently and must not eat the game. It carries it carefully back in a **soft mouth**.

In the international dog organisation FCI, the **retrievers** form a group of their own together with flushing dogs and water dogs. These include the Labrador Retriever, the Golden Retriever and the Flat-coated Retriever. Other breeds are the Chesapeake Bay Retriever, the Curly-coated Retriever and the Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retriever. Labradors come in black, yellow and brown, while Golden Retrievers have long, golden fur.

Because retrievers are calm, friendly and eager to learn, many work as **guide dogs for the blind**. In Switzerland the guide dog school in Allschwil in the canton of Basel-Landschaft trains mainly Labradors. Retrievers also help as rescue dogs, therapy dogs or sniffer dogs at customs. Their good nose and their willingness to work together make them ideal for this.

Retrievers need plenty of exercise and things to do. Long walks, swimming and search games give them great pleasure. Instead of sticks, which dogs can hurt themselves on, balls or special cloth **dummies** are better. Because Labradors like to eat a lot, you should keep an eye on their weight.

begriffe.erklaerung: Fetching an object and bringing it back.
The English word for a dog that retrieves, it means roughly one who fetches back.
A small cloth bag that is thrown in training and brought back by the dog.
A specially trained dog that shows blind people the way safely.

gewusst: A well-trained retriever can carry a raw egg in its mouth without it breaking.
The Labrador Retriever has been one of the most popular family dogs in the world for years.
Labradors have a kind of webbing between the toes that helps when swimming.

teile.einleitung: The Atlantic ridley sea turtle, also called Kemp's ridley, is regarded as one of the smallest sea turtles in the world. It lives mainly in the Gulf of Mexico and is famous for its mass arrivals to lay eggs. At the same time it is one of the most threatened turtles of all.
wichtigste: The Atlantic ridley sea turtle is one of the smallest sea turtles.
Its scientific name is Lepidochelys kempii.
It lives mainly in the Gulf of Mexico and on the Atlantic coast of North America.
The females often come ashore in large groups at the same time to lay eggs.
Unlike most sea turtles, it mostly lays its eggs during the day.
The species is critically endangered and strictly protected.

abschnitte.text: The Atlantic ridley sea turtle is one of the smallest **sea turtles**. Its shell is only about 60 to 70 centimetres long and almost as wide as it is long. Adult animals usually weigh around 35 to 45 kilograms. In adult animals the upper shell is grey-green and the lower shell pale yellowish.

The species lives mainly in the **Gulf of Mexico**, but young animals also swim along the east coast of the USA far to the north. It likes to stay in shallow water with a sandy or muddy bottom. Occasionally young animals are carried by ocean currents as far as the coasts of Europe. Almost all females lay their eggs on beaches in the Mexican state of Tamaulipas.

This turtle's favourite food is **crabs**, which it cracks with its strong horny beak. It also eats mussels, snails, jellyfish and sometimes fish. It usually looks for its prey on the seabed. Its strong jaws are well made for breaking hard shells.

The females often come ashore in their hundreds at the same time to lay their eggs. This mass event is called an **arribada**, which is Spanish and means arrival. Each female digs a pit with her hind flippers and lays about 100 eggs in it. After about seven to eight weeks the young hatch and crawl straight to the sea.

In the past, tens of thousands of females came ashore on a single day at the main beach, Rancho Nuevo in Mexico. Through the collecting of eggs and through fishing nets in which the animals drowned, the population collapsed. Today the nests are guarded, and in many areas fishermen have to use nets with **escape openings** for turtles. The species still counts as critically endangered.

begriffe.erklaerung: A turtle that lives in the sea and has flippers instead of feet.
The mass arrival of many female turtles to lay eggs on the same beach.
A large bay of the sea between the USA, Mexico and Cuba.
The highest level of threat for animals that still live in the wild.

gewusst: The name Kemp's ridley recalls Richard Kemp, a fisherman from Florida who sent animals to researchers.
Whether an egg hatches into a male or a female depends on the temperature in the sand.

teile.einleitung: The Asian tiger mosquito is a small, black-and-white striped mosquito that originally comes from South-East Asia. For some years now it has also been found in the south of Switzerland and is spreading further. It bites mainly during the day and can transmit diseases in warm countries.
wichtigste: You can best recognise the Asian tiger mosquito by its black-and-white stripes.
It originally comes from South and South-East Asia.
For some years now it has also been found in the south of Switzerland.
It was spread mainly with old car tyres and plants.
Unlike many native mosquitoes, it also bites during the day.
It can transmit diseases such as dengue fever or chikungunya.
Anyone who avoids standing water in the garden helps to fight it.

abschnitte.text: The Asian tiger mosquito is smaller than a centimetre and deep black. Its legs and body have striking **white stripes**, hence the name. A single white stripe along the back is also typical. Its scientific name is **Aedes albopictus**.

The tiger mosquito originally lives in the forests of South and South-East Asia. Through world trade its eggs reached many countries in old **car tyres** and ornamental plants. The eggs even survive drought for months. In Europe it was found first in Albania and then in Italy, from where it spread further.

In Switzerland the tiger mosquito was first discovered in 2003 in **Ticino**. By now it is widespread there and also occurs in parts of the Grisons. For some years it has also been found north of the Alps, for example in Basel and in the Zurich region. The cantons monitor its spread with special traps.

Only the females bite, because they need blood for the development of their eggs. The tiger mosquito is a **day-active** mosquito and often bites in the morning and in the late afternoon. It lays its eggs in small collections of water, for example in plant pot saucers, watering cans or rain barrels. After only about a week new mosquitoes can hatch from them.

In tropical countries the tiger mosquito transmits disease germs such as **dengue**, chikungunya or Zika. To do so it first has to bite a sick person, for example someone who caught the infection on a trip. In Italy and France there have already been a few outbreaks. In Switzerland the risk is so far low, but the authorities are watching the situation closely.

The best measure is to avoid **standing water** around the house. Saucers, buckets and toys should be emptied or turned over regularly. Rain barrels should be covered with a tight lid or net. Against bites, light-coloured long clothing and mosquito repellent help.

begriffe.erklaerung: An insect whose females suck blood.
A living thing that has been brought into a foreign area and spreads strongly there.
A disease from tropical countries that is spread by mosquitoes.
An animal that is mainly on the move during the day.

gewusst: Even a bottle cap filled with water is enough for the tiger mosquito as a nursery.
The tiger mosquito usually flies only a few hundred metres, but likes to travel as a stowaway in cars.
In Ticino, trials are being made with releasing sterile males so that the females have no offspring.

teile.einleitung: Species conservation means saving animals and plants from extinction. It includes laws, protected areas and breeding programmes in zoos. Some severely threatened species can today only be saved this way, because they have almost disappeared in the wild.
wichtigste: Species conservation aims to prevent animal and plant species from dying out.
Severely threatened species can sometimes only be saved in zoos or protected areas.
The Red List shows how badly a species is endangered.
The Washington Convention (CITES) regulates worldwide trade in endangered species.
The most important protection is preserving habitats.
In Switzerland the ibex, the beaver and the bearded vulture have been successfully reintroduced.
Each and every one of us can contribute to species conservation.

abschnitte.text: **Species conservation** means all the measures that are meant to preserve threatened animals and plants. This includes protecting habitats such as forests, bogs and rivers. Hunting and trade in rare species are also restricted or banned. The aim is for the species to be able to live in nature again in stable numbers.

The International Union for Conservation of Nature, **IUCN**, which has its seat in Gland in the canton of Vaud, publishes the worldwide **Red List**. In it, species are classed, for example, as vulnerable, endangered or critically endangered. Switzerland also has its own Red Lists for its animals and plants. They show where protection is especially urgent.

The **Washington Convention on endangered species**, CITES for short, was concluded in 1973. It regulates international trade in more than 40,000 species of animals and plants. Its secretariat is in Geneva. Anyone who brings, for example, ivory or protected corals into Switzerland as a souvenir is committing an offence.

When a species has almost disappeared in nature, **breeding programmes** in zoos help. Zoos exchange animals with each other so that the animals are not too closely related. The Przewalski's horse was extinct in the wild and was released again in Mongolia thanks to zoo animals. Zurich Zoo and Basel Zoo also take part in such programmes.

The **ibex** was wiped out in Switzerland in the 19th century. From 1906 young animals from Italy were brought to the Peter and Paul wildlife park in St Gallen and later released. Today about 18,000 ibex live in the Swiss Alps again. The beaver and the **bearded vulture**, which has been released in the National Park and elsewhere since 1991, have also returned.

Everyone can do something for species conservation in everyday life. A garden with native plants and wild corners helps insects, birds and hedgehogs. When shopping you can look for quality labels for sustainable fish and wood. You should also not buy souvenirs made from protected animals or plants.

begriffe.erklaerung: A group of living things that can reproduce with one another.
A list that shows how badly animal and plant species are threatened.
The Washington Convention, which regulates trade in endangered species.
When animals are set free from human care into the wild.

gewusst: The first ibex for the reintroduction in Switzerland were secretly smuggled out of Italy.
The International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN), which publishes the Red List, has its headquarters in Switzerland.
The California condor survived only because in 1987 the last wild animals were caught and bred in zoos.

teile.einleitung: The aurochs was a huge wild bovine that once lived in large parts of Europe, Asia and North Africa. Our cows today are descended from it. It has been extinct for almost 400 years.
wichtigste: The aurochs, also called the “Ur”, was a wild bovine.
Our domestic cows are descended from the aurochs.
The scientific name is Bos primigenius.
Bulls reached a shoulder height of about 1.6 to 1.8 metres.
The last known animal died in 1627 in Poland.
Stone Age people painted aurochs on cave walls, for example at Lascaux in France.

abschnitte.text: The aurochs, also called the **Ur**, was much bigger than most cows today. The bulls had a shoulder height of about 1.6 to 1.8 metres and could weigh around a tonne. They were blackish brown with a pale stripe on the back, while the cows were smaller and reddish brown. Both had large **horns** that curved forwards.

Aurochs lived in open woodland, river meadows and damp grasslands. Their range stretched from Europe through the Near East to India and North Africa. They ate grasses, herbs, leaves and acorns. In Switzerland their bones have been found at many sites from the Stone Age, including in **pile-dwelling settlements**.

About 10,000 years ago people in the **Near East** began to tame aurochs. Over many generations this developed into domestic cattle. In India, too, one form of the aurochs was tamed, and from it came the zebu with its hump. The tamed cattle became smaller and calmer than their wild ancestors.

Through hunting and because forests were turned into fields and pastures, the aurochs disappeared little by little. At the end they lived only in a forest near **Jaktorów** in Poland, where they were protected by kings. In 1627 the last known cow died there. The aurochs is one of the first animals whose extinction was recorded exactly.

In the 1920s and 1930s the Heck brothers in Germany tried to breed aurochs again from domestic cattle. The result is called **Heck cattle**, but it resembles the Ur only in part. Today there are other breeding projects that cross cattle with the most primitive features possible. Some of these cattle are used in nature reserves to keep landscapes open.

begriffe.erklaerung: Another name for the aurochs.
Taming and breeding wild animals into domestic animals.
A breed of cattle that is meant to look like the aurochs.
Stone Age settlements on the shores of lakes, including in Switzerland.

gewusst: The Stone Age paintings in the cave of Lascaux show aurochs that are painted more than five metres long.
In the past, drinking horns for feasts were made from the horns of aurochs.
In the coat of arms of the canton of Uri you can see a bull's head, which is often linked with the Ur.

teile.einleitung: The axolotl is a Mexican salamander that looks like a larva all its life. With its feathery gills and its smiling face it is known around the world. It can also regrow lost body parts completely.
wichtigste: The axolotl is called Ambystoma mexicanum scientifically and belongs to the salamanders and newts.
It belongs to the family of mole salamanders and is closely related to the tiger salamander.
It becomes sexually mature as a larva, which is called neoteny.
It breathes with three pairs of external gills, through the skin and with simple lungs.
When grown it is usually about 20 to 30 centimetres long.
It is endemic to Mexico and naturally lived only in Lake Xochimilco and Lake Chalco.
In the wild it is critically endangered today.

abschnitte.text: The axolotl belongs to the **salamanders and newts**, that is, to the same group of amphibians as newts and salamanders. Its family is the mole salamanders, and it is closely related to the North American **tiger salamander**. Other salamanders change from water larva to land animal, but the axolotl does not. It becomes an adult as a larva and has young, a phenomenon called **neoteny**.

A full-grown axolotl is usually about 20 to 30 centimetres long. On its head it has three pairs of external, feather-like **gill branches** with which it takes oxygen from the water. In addition it breathes through the skin and has simple lungs with which it sometimes gulps air at the surface. Its small eyes have no lids. Wild animals are dark grey-brown, but in aquariums there are also pink-white, golden and black forms.

The axolotl is **endemic** to Mexico, that is, it occurs naturally only there in the whole world. It originally lived only in Lake Xochimilco and Lake Chalco near Mexico City. Lake Chalco was almost completely drained, and in the canals of **Xochimilco** the water is often polluted. Added to this are introduced fish such as carp and cichlids that eat young axolotls.

If an axolotl loses a leg, it grows back completely, with bones, muscles and nerves. It can even restore parts of the heart, spinal cord and eye. That is why scientists around the world study how this **regeneration** works. They hope one day to learn something from it for medicine for people.

Normally the axolotl stays in the water all its life. But if it is given the thyroid hormone **thyroxine**, it can change into a land salamander. Then it loses its gills and the fin fringe on its tail. Such transformed animals, however, usually live for a shorter time.

In the old Aztec empire the axolotl was a food and was linked with the god Xolotl, to whom its name is also traced back. Today it is a popular animal in aquariums and laboratories all over the world. While it is very common in captivity, only a few are left in the wild. It is therefore on the Red List as **critically endangered**.

begriffe.erklaerung: Sexual maturity in the larval stage, without changing into an adult animal.
Breathing organs with which animals take oxygen from the water.
Occurs naturally only in one particular area of the world.
A hormone of the thyroid gland that controls the transformation of amphibians.
The regrowing of lost body parts.

gewusst: An axolotl is shown on a Mexican 50-peso banknote.
In captivity an axolotl can live to be 10 to 15 years old.
Because it can renew parts of its brain and heart, it is one of the most studied animals in regeneration research.

teile.einleitung: Cheek pouches are stretchy pouches in the cheeks of some animals in which they keep food for a time. They are best known in hamsters and chipmunks. But baboons and other monkeys also have such handy storage pouches.
wichtigste: Cheek pouches are skin sacs in the cheeks that serve as transport and storage bags.
Hamsters and chipmunks stuff grains and seeds into them to carry to their burrow.
Baboons keep food in them for a time.
In hamsters the full cheek pouches reach as far as the shoulders.
Pocket gophers have cheek pouches that lie on the outside of the head and are lined with fur.
Cheek pouches help animals to collect a lot of food quickly and eat it in a safe place.

abschnitte.text: Cheek pouches are stretchy **skin sacs** on the inside or outside of the cheeks. Animals can collect food in them without swallowing it straight away. They work like a built-in shopping bag. Later the animals take the food out again with their paws or tongue.

The **hamster** is the best-known animal with cheek pouches. When they are completely full, its cheek pouches reach as far as the shoulders and make the head look twice as wide. In autumn the European hamster in this way drags several kilograms of grain into its burrow as a **winter store**. The chipmunk from North America also transports nuts and seeds in this way.

Baboons, macaques and guenons belong to a group of monkeys that are also called **cheek-pouch monkeys**. With them they can quickly collect a lot when searching for food. Then they retreat to a safe place and eat in peace. That way they do not have to argue with their own kind or with enemies over every single fruit.

abschnitte.titel: Pouches on the outside of the head
abschnitte.text: In the North American **pocket gophers** and pocket mice the cheek pouches lie on the outside of the head. They are lined with fur and open beside the mouth. The animals can even turn them inside out to empty them. That way no soil stays in the mouth when they dig underground.

With cheek pouches an animal can collect a lot of food in a short time and so cut down the time outside when it is exposed to enemies. Animals that lay down **stores** especially benefit from them. The food is hardly digested in the pouches, because these produce no digestive juices. That is why the animals can later take it out again almost unchanged.

begriffe.erklaerung: A stretchy skin sac in the cheek for carrying food.
Food that an animal keeps for later, for example for the winter.
A group of monkeys to which baboons, macaques and guenons belong.
A North American rodent with fur-lined cheek pouches on the outside of its head.

gewusst: The German word “hamstern” for building up stores comes from the hamster and its stuffed cheeks.
The platypus also has cheek pouches in which it collects small animals it has found before it surfaces.

teile.einleitung: The Appenzeller Spitzhauben chicken is a well-known Swiss breed of chicken with a striking crest of feathers on the head. The crest points forwards and is reminiscent of the headgear of the old Appenzell women's costume. The chicken is light, nimble and used to life in the mountains.
wichtigste: The Appenzeller Spitzhauben chicken is a well-known Swiss breed of chicken.
On its head it wears a striking, pointed crest of feathers.
The name comes from a cap of the Appenzell women's costume.
The best-known colour is silver-spangled black.
A hen lays about 150 to 180 white eggs a year.
The birds are weatherproof and like to fly up into trees.
The breed is one of the old Swiss breeds of farm animals.

abschnitte.text: The most striking feature is the pointed **crest of feathers** on the head, pointing forwards. Instead of a serrated comb the birds have a small, two-part **V-shaped comb** that looks like a V. The best-known colour is silver-spangled black, but there are also golden, black and blue birds. The chickens are slim and light and walk with a proud, upright gait.

The breed comes from the **Appenzell region** in eastern Switzerland and has been kept there for centuries. Its name comes from the Spitzhaube, a cap that used to be part of the traditional costume of Appenzell women. The chickens' crest of feathers is reminiscent of this headgear. This makes it a true Swiss breed of chicken.

A hen lays about 150 to 180 white eggs a year. A hen usually weighs only about 1.5 kilograms, a cockerel a little more. The breed is therefore not suited to producing a lot of meat. Today it is bred mainly by hobby keepers for its beauty and hardiness.

Appenzeller Spitzhauben are lively, curious and watchful chickens. They are very **hardy** and cope well with the rough mountain climate. Because they are light, they can fly well and like to perch in trees or on fences. They need plenty of room to roam, where they can scratch about and look for worms and grains.

In the 20th century the old native breeds became rarer and rarer, because high-performance chickens lay more eggs. Since the 1980s the foundation **Pro Specie Rara** has been working to preserve old Swiss breeds of farm animals, including the Appenzeller Spitzhauben. Thanks to dedicated breeders the breed is now secure again. At poultry shows in Switzerland it is a popular eye-catcher.

begriffe.erklaerung: A group of domestic animals of the same species with shared, bred characteristics.
A tuft of long feathers on the head of a bird.
A small comb made of two points that look like little horns.
A Swiss foundation that preserves old breeds of farm animals and cultivated plants.

gewusst: The crest of feathers can be so big that it takes away a little of the chickens' view.
There is a second Appenzell breed of chicken, the Appenzeller Barthuhn, which has a beard of feathers.
Appenzeller Spitzhauben fly so well that their run often has to be covered with a net.

teile.einleitung: The blackbird is one of the best-known birds in Switzerland. The male is black with a bright orange-yellow beak. With its beautiful, fluting song it often wakes us at first light.
wichtigste: The blackbird belongs to the thrush family.
The male is black, the female dark brown.
Many males have a yellow ring around the eyes.
Blackbirds live in gardens, parks and woods.
In summer they especially like to eat worms and insects, in autumn berries.
A blackbird raises two to three broods a year.
Many Swiss blackbirds stay nearby in winter.

abschnitte.text: The **blackbird** (Turdus merula) is about 24 to 27 centimetres long and weighs around 100 grams. The male is all black and has a bright orange-yellow **beak**. Many males wear a yellow ring around the eyes. The female is dark brown with a slightly spotted breast, which makes her better camouflaged on the nest. The legs are dark brown to blackish.

Originally the blackbird was a shy **woodland bird**. In the 19th century it began to move into towns and villages. Today in Switzerland it mostly lives in gardens, parks, cemeteries and woods. It is one of the best-known and most common garden birds. You can find it from the lowlands up to the mountain forests.

In summer blackbirds especially like to eat **earthworms**, insects, larvae and snails. You often see them hopping across the lawn, tilting their head to one side and then striking in a flash. In autumn and winter they eat many berries and fruits, for example elder, rowan berries and apples. In doing so they spread the seeds of shrubs. When they search through dry leaves you often hear a soft rustling.

In spring the male sings from high places such as roof ridges, aerials and treetops. His **song** is loud, fluting and melodic. The blackbird is often one of the first to sing at first light, and it also sings in the evening twilight. When danger threatens, it calls loudly and quickly “tix-tix-tix”. When it flies off in alarm, you often hear a shrill chattering.

The female builds a nest of grass, twigs and earth in hedges, trees or even on house walls. She usually lays four to five blue-green, speckled eggs. After about two weeks the young hatch, and both parents feed them. After around two more weeks the young birds leave the nest before they can really fly, and are then called **fledglings**. A blackbird can raise young two to three times a year.

In Switzerland the blackbird is a **resident bird** or partial migrant. Many birds stay nearby in winter or only travel short distances, and they do not fly far into Africa. Their enemies include house cats, sparrowhawks, magpies and crows. Since about 2016, in some summers many blackbirds in Switzerland have died of the **Usutu virus**, which is spread by mosquitoes. With hedges, bushes and a garden close to nature you can help blackbirds.

begriffe.erklaerung: A family of songbirds that includes the blackbird, the song thrush and the fieldfare.
A bird that stays in the same area all year round.
A young bird that has left the nest but cannot yet fly well.
A disease-causing germ that is spread by mosquitoes and can kill many blackbirds.

gewusst: Blackbirds in towns often sing earlier in the morning than in the woods, because it is brighter and noisier there.
There are also blackbirds with white feathers, which happens because of a disturbance in the making of pigment.
Some blackbirds copy other birds or even mobile phone ringtones in their song.

teile.einleitung: The Appenzell goat is a Swiss breed of goat from eastern Switzerland with a snow-white coat. Typical of it are the upright ears. At the cattle processions up to the mountain pastures in the Appenzell region, the white goats often walk proudly at the head of the procession.
wichtigste: The Appenzell goat is a Swiss breed of goat.
Its coat is entirely white.
Typical are the upright ears.
Most animals have no horns.
It is kept mainly for its milk.
At the procession up to the mountain pastures in the Appenzell region the goats often lead the way.
The breed was rare and is supported by Pro Specie Rara.

abschnitte.text: The Appenzell goat has a **white** coat that is often quite long. Especially on the hind legs, the long hair forms a kind of trousers. The ears stand upright and point slightly forwards. Most animals are **hornless**, that is, born without horns. A full-grown nanny goat (“Geiss”) weighs about 45 kilograms, a billy goat considerably more.

The breed comes from the cantons of **Appenzell Innerrhoden** and Appenzell Ausserrhoden and from the area around St Gallen. Farming families there have kept white goats for a long time. The animals are well adapted to the hilly and steep terrain. They climb surely and find enough food even on steep slopes.

Appenzell goats are good **dairy goats**. A nanny goat gives several hundred litres of milk a year. From goat's milk you can make cheese, yoghurt and other dairy products. Goats also help to keep pastures open, because they eat bushes and shrubs as well.

A special moment is the **procession up to the mountain pastures** (“Alpfahrt”) in early summer, when the cattle move up to the high pasture. In the Appenzell region the white goats often walk at the front. They are accompanied by a child in traditional costume, the “Geissbub” or “Geissmeitli”, the goat boy or goat girl. Behind them follow the herdsmen in their festive costume and the cows with large bells.

In the 20th century the Appenzell goat became rarer and rarer, because other breeds gave more milk. The foundation **Pro Specie Rara** took the breed into its conservation programme. Today many farms are breeding this goat again. It is a piece of living cultural heritage of eastern Switzerland.

begriffe.erklaerung: The Swiss word for a female goat.
A male goat.
Without horns, as many Appenzell goats are by nature.
The procession in which the animals are taken up to the mountain pastures in early summer.

gewusst: Goats are among the oldest domestic animals and were tamed some 10,000 years ago.
Goats like to eat buds and leaves from shrubs and even stand on their hind legs to reach them.
The white goats at the head of the Appenzell procession up to the mountain pastures are a popular photo subject.

teile.einleitung: The Andes are the longest mountain range in the world above sea level. They run like a giant backbone along the whole west coast of South America. Llamas come from here, the Incas lived here and here stands the highest mountain outside Asia.
wichtigste: The Andes are about 7,500 kilometres long.
They stretch through seven countries, from Venezuela to Chile and Argentina.
The highest mountain is Aconcagua in Argentina at 6,961 metres.
There are many active volcanoes in the Andes.
Llamas, alpacas, vicuñas and the Andean condor live here.
The Inca Empire had its centre in the Andes.
Potatoes originally come from the Andes.

abschnitte.text: The **Andes** stretch about 7,500 kilometres from the Caribbean coast in the north to Tierra del Fuego in the south. That is about seven times as long as the Alps. They pass through Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, Bolivia, Chile and Argentina. In places the Andes are more than 500 kilometres wide. In Peru and Bolivia the high plateau called the **Altiplano** lies between two mountain chains.

The highest mountain in the Andes is **Aconcagua** in Argentina at 6,961 metres. It is the highest mountain outside Asia. The Andes are formed because the Nazca Plate is pushing under the South American continent. That is why there are many **volcanoes** and earthquakes here, for example Cotopaxi in Ecuador. The summit of Chimborazo in Ecuador is the point on the Earth's surface that is farthest from the centre of the Earth.

The Andes have very different landscapes, from rainforests and glaciers to deserts. In the north the mountain slopes are damp and green. On the border between Chile and Peru lies the **Atacama**, one of the driest deserts on Earth. Right in the south, in Patagonia, there are huge glaciers and ice fields. At great heights it is cold, and the air contains little oxygen.

**Llamas** and alpacas originally live in the Andes, and they are descended from the wild guanacos and vicuñas. Llamas have been used as pack animals for thousands of years, alpacas mainly for their wool. Above the peaks soars the **Andean condor**, one of the largest flying birds with a wingspan of around three metres. Other residents are the spectacled bear, the chinchilla and many species of hummingbird. Some of these animals are found nowhere else.

In the 15th and early 16th centuries the **Incas** ruled a large empire in the Andes with its capital at Cusco in Peru. The ruined city of **Machu Picchu**, high above a valley, is famous. The Incas built terraced fields and a long network of roads through the mountains. To this day many people in the Andes speak Quechua or Aymara. Potatoes, quinoa and tomatoes originally come from this region.

Some of the highest cities in the world lie in the Andes. La Paz in Bolivia lies at about 3,600 metres, Quito in Ecuador at around 2,800 metres. The people in the high regions have adapted to the thin air. Copper, silver, gold and lithium are mined in the mountains. For mountaineers, including those from Switzerland, the Andes are a popular destination.

begriffe.erklaerung: A long chain of high mountains.
A mountain from which hot, liquid rock, called lava, can escape.
A huge piece of the Earth's crust that moves very slowly.
A people who ruled a large empire in the Andes more than 500 years ago.

gewusst: The summit of Chimborazo is farther from the centre of the Earth than the summit of Mount Everest, because the Earth is thicker at the equator.
The Incas sent messages with runners who took turns along their mountain roads.
A llama spits when it is annoyed, but mostly at other llamas.

teile.einleitung: Arachnology is the science that deals with spiders and their relatives. People who do research in this field study how spiders are built, how they live and how they weave their webs. The name comes from the Greek word “arachne” for spider.
wichtigste: Arachnology is the science of spiders and arachnids.
Researchers in this field are called arachnologists.
Besides spiders, arachnids include scorpions, harvestmen and mites.
More than 50,000 species of spider have been described worldwide.
Around 1,000 species of spider live in Switzerland.
Arachnologists also study spider silk and spider venoms.
Arachnology is a branch of zoology.

abschnitte.text: **Arachnology** is a branch of zoology, the study of animals. It deals with the **arachnids**, which have eight legs and a two-part body. They include web-building spiders, scorpions, harvestmen, pseudoscorpions and mites. Insects such as beetles or flies are not included, because they have only six legs.

Arachnologists collect spiders in nature, for example with traps on the ground or by tapping branches. With the **microscope** they study fine features such as eyes, hairs and reproductive organs, by which species are told apart. Today analyses of DNA also help to tell related species apart. Every year, hundreds of new species of spider are still discovered.

A major research topic is **spider silk**, which, in proportion to its weight, is stronger than steel. Researchers hope to make new materials for medicine and technology from it one day. **Spider venoms** are also studied, because some substances in them may be useful as medicines. Other arachnologists observe how spiders hunt, build webs or look after their young.

The name goes back to the Greek legend of **Arachne**, a weaver who was turned into a spider by the goddess Athena. An important milestone was the book “Svenska Spindlar” by the Swede Carl Alexander Clerck from 1757. In it, spiders were for the first time given scientific names according to the system that is usual today. Today the World Spider Catalog at the Natural History Museum of Bern collects all the known species of spider in the world.

Around 1,000 species of spider occur in Switzerland. Well known are the **garden spider**, the house spider and the cellar spider. No native spider is dangerous to people. Spiders are useful because they eat very many insects such as mosquitoes and flies.

begriffe.erklaerung: The science of spiders and their relatives.
Animals with eight legs, for example spiders, scorpions and mites.
The science that deals with animals.
A great fear of spiders.

gewusst: The World Spider Catalog, the most important list of all spider species, is looked after in Bern.
The fear of spiders is called arachnophobia and is one of the most common fears.
All the spiders in the world together are estimated to eat hundreds of millions of tonnes of insects every year.

teile.einleitung: The brown trout is a typical fish of clear, cold streams and rivers and one of the best-known fish of Switzerland. You recognise it by its red and black spots. Because it needs clean, oxygen-rich water, it shows whether a body of water is healthy.
wichtigste: The brown trout lives in cold, flowing, clean water.
On its body it usually has red and black spots.
Most brown trout lay their eggs in autumn and winter.
Trout eggs need cool, oxygen-rich water.
The lake trout belongs to the same species, but lives in the lake.
In the wild a brown trout lives for about 5 to 10 years.
Dams are a problem because the fish can no longer reach their spawning grounds.

abschnitte.text: The brown trout, in Latin **Salmo trutta fario**, belongs, like the salmon, to the salmon family. Its back is usually brownish or olive green, and on its sides it has red and black spots that are often ringed with a pale border. In streams it usually grows to 20 to 40 centimetres long, in large rivers also more. On its back it has, like all salmonids, a small **adipose fin** without fin rays.

Brown trout like cold, flowing water with plenty of oxygen, as in mountain streams and the upper reaches of rivers. During the day, when it is very bright, it often hides in the shade under stones, roots or overhanging banks. It swims fastest with powerful movements of its tail. In polluted or too warm water, trout get into trouble and can die, which is why they count as an **indicator species** for healthy waters.

Brown trout eat insect larvae, freshwater shrimps, worms and insects that fall into the water. Large animals also hunt small fish. Young trout are often hunted by **grey herons** and the kingfisher. Goosanders, cormorants and otters also eat trout.

Most brown trout spawn in autumn and winter. The female beats a pit into the gravel with her tail, a so-called **redd**, and lays the eggs there. The eggs need cool, oxygen-rich water that flows through the gravel. After a few weeks the **alevins** hatch, which at first feed on their yolk sac on the belly.

The brown trout occurs in Switzerland in almost all streams from the Central Plateau up into the Alps. The **lake trout** belongs to the same species, but grows up in the lake and migrates into the inflowing streams to spawn. In recent decades the populations have fallen sharply in many places. The reasons are warmer water, diseases, river engineering and power stations that block the migration to the spawning grounds.

begriffe.erklaerung: Laying eggs and fertilising them, in fish and amphibians.
A store of nutrients on the belly of a newly hatched fish larva.
An animal or plant whose presence shows the condition of the environment.
A form of the trout that lives in the lake and migrates into rivers to spawn.

gewusst: Lake trout can grow to more than a metre long, much bigger than brown trout in a stream.
Depending on the water, the same species of trout can be very differently coloured, almost silvery or very dark.

teile.einleitung: The ampullae of Lorenzini are tiny sense organs on the snouts of sharks and rays. With them the animals can sense very weak electrical signals sent out by other living things. This “sixth sense” helps sharks to find even prey that is hidden in the sand.
wichtigste: The ampullae of Lorenzini are sense organs for electric fields.
They sit mainly on the snout and head of sharks and rays.
You can see them as small pores in the skin.
The pores lead to canals filled with a gel.
Every living thing produces weak electrical signals, for example with its heartbeat and muscle movements.
They are named after the Italian Stefano Lorenzini, who described them in 1678.
Sharks are among the animals with the finest electrical sense.

abschnitte.text: The **ampullae of Lorenzini** are small sense organs in the skin of sharks, rays and chimaeras. From the outside you can only see tiny holes, the **pores**, often scattered like freckles over the snout. Each pore leads into a canal filled with a clear gel. At the end of the canal there is a small bulb, the ampulla, with sensory cells. A shark can have hundreds to thousands of these ampullae.

abschnitte.titel: How does the electrical sense work?
abschnitte.text: All animals produce weak electrical voltages, for example with every heartbeat, with muscle movements and when breathing. In salty seawater these **electric fields** spread out a little. The gel in the canals carries the voltage very well to the sensory cells. These report to the brain where the source is. In this way the shark can sense voltages that are many thousands of times weaker than those of a small battery.

With the **electrical sense**, sharks and rays find prey over the last few centimetres, even when they cannot see anything. A flatfish buried in the sand gives itself away by the movements of its gills. **Hammerhead sharks** have their ampullae spread across their whole broad head and use them to sweep the seabed like a metal detector. Just before biting, many sharks close their eyes or protect them, and then only the electrical sense helps them. Sharks may also use these organs to find their way by the Earth's magnetic field.

The Italian doctor **Stefano Lorenzini** described the organs in 1678 in an electric ray. But he did not know what they were for. For a long time researchers thought they measured pressure or temperature. Only around 1960 did scientists find out that they are sense organs for electric fields. Since then the electrical sense has also been discovered in other animals.

Some other animals also sense electric fields, such as sturgeons, catfish and many lungfish. The **platypus** in Australia uses electroreceptors in its bill to find worms and crustaceans in the mud. Even bumblebees can detect electric charges on flowers. Researchers use this knowledge to develop electric **shark deterrents** for surfers and divers. These send out strong electrical signals that disturb the sharks' electrical sense.

begriffe.erklaerung: A part of the body with which a living thing notices something in its surroundings, for example an eye or an ear.
An invisible region around an electrical voltage that can be measured.
A tiny opening in the skin.
A sensory cell that detects electrical signals.

gewusst: The gel in the ampullae of Lorenzini is one of the best conductors of electricity ever found in animals.
Sharks sometimes bite undersea cables, perhaps because they mistake their electric fields for prey.
